exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
cohort: 301 women after childbirth (234 vaginal, 67 cesarean section)
finding: The Postpartum Functional Assessment Questionnaire demonstrated good psychometric properties and revealed significant differences in pain intensity and functional abilities between women who had vaginal deliveries and those who had cesarean sections, with improvements observed from day 1 to day 3 postpartum in both groups.
mod_finding: Women who underwent cesarean sections experienced significantly higher pain intensity and lower functional abilities compared to those who had vaginal deliveries.
